novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 flagship framing
novelty_flags.one_line: The Stat-cluster kernels give an exact decision-game solution and a conditional regret-transfer inequality, but neither states a rate/lower bound, sharper published bound, efficiency result, coverage result, nor first nontrivial statistical bound, so they cap at field.

soundness_flags.label: ass:nontrivial-sign-ambiguity
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited paper's formal nontrivial-partial-identification condition requires an open set of reduced-form values, not merely one sign-ambiguous h₀; retag this weaker condition or strengthen it.

soundness_flags.label: ass:joint-risk-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: Uniform joint total-variation approximation of a data-dependent statistic and estimated game is not the standard Le Cam condition supplied by HiranoPorter2009; make it a novel, independently justified sample-splitting/stable-construction condition.

soundness_flags.label: prop:certificate-convergence
soundness_flags.one_line: “Weak-star limit point of δ_m” is undefined because no weak-star topology or ambient L∞ space is specified for the Lebesgue-a.e. quotient rule class.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies reference PDF, January 2026
source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 7, Definition 2 (lines 271–280 in extracted PDF text)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited paper defines nontrivial partial identification by existence of an open set S such that the identified interval straddles zero throughout S; this is stronger than existence of one h₀ with ℓ(h₀)<0<u(h₀).

The paper develops treatment-rule asymptotics through limits of experiments in smooth parametric and semiparametric models; it does not state the proposal's joint-TV approximation for a sample-derived Gaussian statistic jointly with a plug-in estimated endpoint game.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Derive γ_n→0 from an explicit sample-split construction, including the conditional Gaussian approximation and estimated-game dependence, rather than assuming it as a condition labelled standard.
Specify D as the unit ball of L∞(Lebesgue) with its weak-star topology, state the representative convention, and formulate the selector-limit claim in that topology.

Keep the decision-theory results field-tier, or add a genuine Stat frontier result: for example a derived rate for estimated endpoint primitives with a named structural modulus and a matching lower bound or strict comparison to an existing feasible rule.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two mislabelled assumptions and the selector topology, then retain the core as a field-tier decision-theory proposal unless a real statistical frontier result is added.
